name: Goulburn Valley

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Malbec and Sangiovese fully without cooking off their freshness.
Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Chardonnay is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Riesling is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water. Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it. Clay holds water well but drains poorly. It stays cool, which slows ripening and keeps acidity up.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Mostly flat. Easy and cheap to farm by machine, but on still nights cold air settles on flat ground, so spring frost is a bigger risk.

winkler: Good for generous crops of standard to good wine.
